sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Type-checking rules
sections.what: Sets how strictly the frontend code is checked and which kinds of mistakes are reported as errors.
sections.why: Likely reason: catches type and leftover-code problems before users see them.
sections.watch_out: A single unused variable can stop the build.

summary: TypeScript rules for the frontend: strict type checking and warnings for unused code.
purpose: Tells the TypeScript checker how strict to be and which files to check.
why: Likely reason: strict checking catches bugs early, and the unused-code rules flag leftovers.
how: Sets the JavaScript target and libraries, uses bundler-style module rules, turns off file output because Vite does the building, enables strict mode and unused-code errors, and checks the src folder. It also refers to a second config file for build tools.
inputs: Files in src and the referenced tsconfig.node.json.
outputs: Type errors reported during build. No output files.
risks: Unused-code rules make the build fail over small leftovers. The referenced tsconfig.node.json is not in the packet, so it may be missing.
debug: When build fails, read the first error. It names the file and line.
